transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-23 10:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Marisol Rivera (Redwood SE), Sam Patel (Acme CTO), Rima Johnson (Cloud Architect), Luca Moretti (Security), Priya Desai (ML Eng)

Summary: quick status sync on Redwood Private VPC pilot — networking, routing, upgrade plan, and tuning notes.
Topics: networking/VPC peering, NAT/egress, private control plane routing, KMS/HSM integration, kernel/agent upgrade schedule, performance tuning (KV cache, batching), next steps/dry-run plan.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we're on for 45 minutes today, quick readout, then go through issues. Sam, Rima, Luca — thanks for making time.
[00:13] Sam: yeah thanks Alex, and hi Marisol, been a busy week, got a couple of blockers on the networking side we want to confirm.
[00:20] Marisol: cool, we'll start with networking, quick recap — last week we asked Acme for staging CIDRs and firewall rules, Rima sent a draft but we saw some holes in the egress rules.
[00:33] Rima: sorry, yes we sent the CIDR list, I meant to correct one of the ranges, we had an overlap with our analytics VPC. It should be 10.20.0.0/16 not 10.2.0.0. Also we had questions on the outbound nat behaviour for calls to artifacts.redwood.cloud.
[00:50] Alex: right the control plane needs outbound to S3 and our metrics collector, also to the compilation service for kernel selection. For the private mode we have an option to mirror the control plane through a bastion or to allow limited egress via a proxy; the proxy option is typically easier for customers with strict egress.
[01:10] Luca: just to call out from security side, we need egress locked down to TLS only and mTLS to the KMS endpoints, plus full audit logs for the control plane actions. Any support for HSMs?
[01:24] Marisol: yes we support external KMS and HSM via the Redwood connector, it's been tested in earlier pilots. There might be config changes in the agent to enable pkcs11. We'll add the details to the runbook.
[01:38] Priya: quick question about secrets — is the agent storing keys locally or is it strictly a pass-through to KMS? We want no long-lived keys on the hosts.
[01:48] Marisol: agent is keyless by default, we do a short-lived token exchange with the KMS; however there was some ambiguity in the current build about caching the token for five minutes, we'll clarify that.
[02:01] Alex: ok action to clarify token lifetime and cert rotation.
[02:06] Sam: on routing, we've configured VPC peering to Redwood staging, but routing tables aren't sending traffic to the dedicated inference instances — it looks like the security group for the inference nodes is dropping traffic from the peering range.
[02:22] Marisol: we saw that in the logs too, there was a default SG applied by the template. We updated the terraform to expose port 443 and our control port 27123, but double-check your egress on your side — sometimes the peering doesn't include the right route table associations.
[02:40] Rima: yep we'll double check, I can share the terraform and route table output after the call.
[02:46] Alex: great, please include the exact flow logs export — that helps us pinpoint where the packet drops are happening.

-- Performance results and tuning --
[03:10] Alex: next, quick perf snapshot from the run we did last night — Marisol, can you summarize?
[03:17] Marisol: sure. We ran the sample embedding and generation pipeline at 2k concurrent sessions in staging. Baseline latency median for short prompts was ~120ms per token on the current quantized variant, p95 around 410ms. Throughput looked good until we hit a memory pressure point where the KV cache thrashes.
[03:38] Priya: memory pressure as in OOM or GC? We saw CPU jump too, and some processes got killed on one node.
[03:45] Marisol: it was eviction, not a full OOM, the runtime evicted KV segments then warmed them again causing stalls. We'll tune the cache size and the IO prefetch. There's also a newer agent we want to push that improves cache eviction heuristics.
[03:58] Sam: how risky is that agent upgrade? We can't afford downtime.
[04:03] Marisol: the upgrade is designed to be canaryed — we can roll to a single node first, route a small percentage of traffic, monitor, then ramp. We'll provide a roll-back script.
[04:15] Alex: good — plan is to do a dry-run in staging then a controlled canary in pre-prod. We should schedule the dry-run next week.

[04:30] Luca: from security perspective, during an upgrade we need to ensure audit logs are preserved and that the node reintrospects keys correctly, not reusing stale sessions. Also, any change that modifies TLS params needs review.
[04:45] Marisol: yes audit log continuity is a requirement. The agent ships a checkpointed state that includes a minimal audit pointer. We're going to add explicit guidance in the upgrade section of the runbook.

-- KMS and encryption deep-dive (short) --
[05:05] Alex: Marisol you said earlier about pkcs11 and HSMs — can you outline the steps?
[05:11] Marisol: the short of it: we integrate via our connector which uses mTLS to the customer's KMS endpoint. For HSMs we support PKCS#11 and we require the appropriate user mapping. There's a small daemon that handles signing requests; it runs in a sidecar. We've seen small service account permission issues in one pilot where the sidecar couldn't access the socket.
[05:31] Priya: sidecar needs unix-socket permissions, got it. We'll check.
[05:35] Rima: any ISO or SOC doc addenda for this? We need to update our compliance reviewers.
[05:40] Alex: yes I'll re-send the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts and include a short note on the HSM connector behavior.

-- Misc/obs and imperfect transcription artifacts --
[05:55] Sam: also curious about costs in dedicated mode vs Private — we had an internal question whether the unit cost per token with the quantized variant on our infra will be cheaper than hosted.
[06:09] Marisol: usually dedicated/reserved capacity is cheaper at scale due to amortized GPU costs, but in private you take on infra ops costs; we can do a cost modeling spreadsheet for you — I'll attach a template.
[06:22] Sam: please do that, and show break-even at our projected 50M tokens/month.

-- Open issues / blockers --
[06:35] Alex: quick list: 1) Networking egress rules and SG fix (Acme/Rima), 2) Agent upgrade dry-run scheduling, 3) KMS HSM permissions and sidecar socket access, 4) Perf run with KV-cache tuning and memory thresholds.
[06:53] Rima: we also noticed the control plane cert validation failed once in the logs — error said "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" — could be our internal root not in the trust store.
[07:06] Marisol: that's likely a trust chain issue, we can accept a CA bundle in the agent config; we need to coordinate the exact PEM format. I'll include sample config.
[07:18] Priya: small nit: we saw some entries in the logs where "KV cache" got transcribed as "K V cash" in the debug UI, might confuse folks reading the auto-generated logs. Not a big deal but FYI.
[07:30] Alex: ha, yup transcription quirks, we'll ignore that in the runbook.

-- Next: upgrade plan specifics --
[07:40] Marisol: proposed plan: 1) push agent v1.13.2 to one staging node, 2) run loadbench at 2k concurrency on that node and compare latency/eviction rates, 3) if stable, canary to 10% of pre-prod traffic, 4) monitor for 24 hours, then ramp. Each step has a rollback.
[08:03] Sam: sounds good, we want a hard "kill switch" in case the cache thrashing resumes — something automatic to flip back to previous image.
[08:11] Marisol: we've got that, our rollout controller can automatically revert if error rate > 3% for 5 mins, but we'll also provide a manual rollback command.

-- Scheduling and runbook items --
[08:25] Alex: can we confirm dates? Rima, you said you'd share route tables today (2026-12-23). For the dry-run week of Jan 6, can you confirm you have capacity?
[08:37] Rima: yes we can take a 2-hour window on Jan 7 for the dry-run. We'll confirm exact windows in the next 48 hours.
[08:44] Sam: and the loadbench — we can run the nightly bench starting 2026-12-28 and share the output by Jan 3.

-- Closing and recap --
[08:55] Alex: recap: Redwood to share updated private-deploy runbook (network diagrams, CA bundle example, KMS notes) by Monday 12/27. Marisol to prepare KV-cache tuning guide and sample manifests by 12/29. Acme to check SG/route table and share flow logs and terraform outputs by 12/28. Luca to enumerate SOC 2 addenda requirements by 12/30. We'll schedule dry-run for week of Jan 6, target Jan 7 for staging dry-run.
[09:25] Luca: from security: one more ask — can Redwood provide an example of audit log schema so our SIEM team can onboard?
[09:33] Alex: yes, we'll include a sample log schema and an example log export in the runbook.
[09:38] Priya: thanks everyone, that was productive.
[09:41] Sam: thanks all, feel good about the plan.
[09:44] Alex: great meeting, we'll follow up with notes and the runbook attachments.

Action items recap (verbatim):
- Alex Chen: send private-deploy runbook + network diagram - due 2026-12-27
- Marisol Rivera: prepare KV-cache tuning guide and sample kube manifests - due 2026-12-29
- Rima Johnson: provide CIDR ranges and VPC peering details for staging - due 2026-12-28

Transcript end.
